page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.8xlarge is an x86_64 server instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is also strong in Geekbench, though stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores align with average tier results. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with Passmark memory scores in the top 25%, supported by a read-only small block cached memory bandwidth of 2464.24 GB/sec. Cryptographic operations perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by a strong Passmark CPU encryption score of 39057.13, aided by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

Lacking local storage, this instance relies entirely on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs compared to local NVMe options. However, its high memory density provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads by reducing the need to scale up to larger, more expensive instance sizes just for RAM. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, 256 GB of RAM, and strong cryptographic and text processing performance makes this instance highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, enterprise applications, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and data processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.8xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps but contains no local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core CPU performance, high memory scores, and excellent cryptographic execution, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AES and SHA_NI. Conversely, multi-core computational tasks and memory bandwidth under large block sizes fall into average performance tiers. Due to its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU and the absence of local storage, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that rely on network storage. It is well-suited for hosting in-memory databases, caching systems, and enterprise applications requiring substantial memory capacity.
